page: The UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at 2.0 GHz with 32 physical cores. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. For hardware acceleration, it bundles two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. No local storage is included in this configuration.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance across multiple compute and processing metrics. The AMD EPYC CPU achieves top 10% scores in both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, as well as Geekbench single-core evaluations. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3 operations, also rank in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is strong, registering 327.05 GB/sec for large-block reads and 126.98 GB/sec for writes. For AI workloads, the dual L40S GPUs enable top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds on small LLM models, though performance scales to average levels when running larger 70B parameter models.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive parallel GPU acceleration paired with substantial system memory. However, the shared CPU allocation model and the complete absence of local storage represent key architectural tradeoffs. Users must provision external storage volumes for data persistence, and workloads highly sensitive to CPU scheduling jitter may need to account for the shared CPU resource model.

This configuration is highly suited for machine learning workloads, specifically LLM inference on small-to-medium models, image processing, and data science pipelines. It is also well-suited for database operations, high-throughput web serving, and software compilation tasks that benefit from the combination of high-capacity system RAM and dual hardware accelerators.

It features an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 32 vCPUs (32 physical cores) on the x86_64 architecture, paired with 384.0 GB of system memory. The server bundles two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, providing a total of 96 GB of VRAM, but does not include local storage. Benchmark data indicates top-tier CPU performance in single-core and multi-core stress tests, alongside strong memory bandwidth. The dual GPUs deliver excellent prompt processing and text generation speeds for small and medium LLM models. Given the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage, this instance is best suited for machine learning inference, image processing, software compilation, and memory-heavy database operations where external storage is utilized.
